source: spec §4.7 'Delivery ladder' and §7 E1 — inline_exact → inline_nearest → file_level → summary_only, and nothing is ever dropped.
notes: Recomputed from the recorded diff by verify_corpus.py, so these rungs cannot drift from the patch. Two of the cases sit either side of the ≤10 boundary on purpose: line 101 is exactly 10 lines from the nearest in-hunk line and stays inline, line 102 is 11 and must demote.

findings.why: The changed line itself: on the RIGHT side, inside a hunk. Rung 1.
Six lines past the end of the hunk. Comment goes on line 91 with the body prefixed '> Nearest reviewable line. The issue is at `app/checkout.py:97`.'
Exactly NEAREST_LINE_MAX_DISTANCE away. The bound is inclusive, so this still goes inline.
One line further than f-nearest-boundary: 11 > 10, so it demotes to a file-level comment with subject_type 'file'.
In a changed file but far from every hunk. Rung 3.
The file is not in the diff at all, so GitHub will not take a comment on it. Rung 4: a row in the review body's 'Findings not attachable to the diff' table — still delivered, never dropped.

conservation: len(published) == inline_exact + inline_nearest + file_level + summary_only == 6. AC-17 requires this assertion to live in production code, not only in a test.

after_422_retry.why: GitHub rejects the comment posted at app/checkout.py:91 — the anchor line chosen for f-nearest-boundary — as not part of the diff. That finding demotes exactly one rung, from inline_nearest to file_level; the whole review is retried once; and the conservation invariant is re-asserted after the retry. Still 6 published, still one review call retried exactly once.
